title: Deep Work, lesson 1 - 5 truths about focus

slides.head: 5 Truths About Focus That Will _Quietly_ Change Your Career
slides.note:
from Deep Work
by Cal Newport

slides.head: You've never been busier.
body: Emails. Pings. Meetings. Twelve open tabs.
You end the day exhausted, yet the work that *actually matters* hasn't moved.

slides.head: The problem isn't you. It's _shallow work_.

terms.def: Emails and logistics you can do half asleep. It keeps you *busy*, but rarely creates anything new.
Concentrating without distraction on something *hard*. Cal Newport says it's becoming a superpower.

slides.title: Everyone's distracted, so focus is now a superpower
slides.what: Most people spend their days constantly connected and interrupted. That makes the few who can focus *worth more than ever*.
slides.try: Ask yourself: _“When did I last work on one thing for an hour, uninterrupted?”_

slides.title: Machines are changing who gets ahead
slides.what: As smart machines reshape work, Newport says the people who get ahead can *learn hard things quickly* and *produce at an elite level*.
slides.try: Pick the one hard skill your career needs most, and give it your focus first.

slides.title: “Quick checks” quietly drain your focus
slides.what: Researcher Sophie Leroy found that when you switch tasks, part of your attention *stays stuck* on the last one. She called it attention residue.
slides.try: Before you check that inbox, ask: _“Does this need me right now?”_

diagram.label:

slides.title: Long hours won't save distracted work
slides.what: Newport's formula: high-quality work equals *time spent × intensity of focus*. Cut the intensity, and extra hours barely help.
slides.try: Ask: _“Would one truly focused hour beat my last three distracted ones?”_

slides.title: One deep skill can rewrite your career
slides.what: Jason Benn's finance job was mostly spreadsheets. He taught himself to code through long, undistracted study, and *became a software developer*.
slides.try: Ask: _“What skill would change my career if I learned it deeply?”_

slides.head: Start tomorrow: protect one hour
steps: Block one hour for your *hardest* task.
Phone in another room. Inbox closed.
slides.challenge: Tonight, look at yesterday honestly: how many hours of true, unbroken focus did you get?

slides.head: Which one hit _hardest_?
slides.body: Save this for your next busy week, and send it to someone who's always “busy”.
